title: Billy Graham's Radio Ministry
text:
Billy Graham's Radio Ministry

# Billy Graham’s Radio Ministry

#### February 6, 2024

World Radio Day is Feb. 13, 2024. Plan your visit to the Billy Graham Library to see how this medium impacted the ministry of Billy Graham.

Billy Graham’s mission in ministry was always to spread the Gospel by every effective means possible. Once his trajectory took him into the broadcast world, he couldn’t turn back. He began reaching millions through radio. So, how did he go from local to national to satellite radio?

#### Early 1940s: First Radio Program

One day, a man named Torrey Johnson called Graham and asked him to take over his 45-minute radio program. It would cost $150 a week for the radio time on WCFL in Chicago. “Little did I realize that it was one of the turning points in my life,” said Graham.

Billy took the request to the deacons of church he pastored, and after the financial needs were provided, they agreed to the offer. He wanted there to be a marquee name on the program, so he invited George Beverly Shea, a bass baritone and a staff announcer at the Moody Bible Institute’s station, WMBI. Shea, after much discussion, finally said he would be part of the program.

“I built my radio talks around the events of the day,” said Graham. “Keeping up with current events through newspapers and radio news programs, I began each message with a reference to something people would have been hearing and talking about that very day. Then I moved into a biblical message, showing that God and the Scriptures are relevant to every problem.”

Billy Graham’s first radio show preformed so well that WMBI signed him and his team to broadcast their regular Sunday morning church service during March and April of 1944.

#### National Broadcast: The Hour of Decision

A few years later, in 1950, Billy was speaking at a conference in Michigan. Two men walked up to him and introduced themselves as Fred Dienert and Walter Bennett. They tried to interest him in a national radio program. At that point in time, he was much too busy to take on an effort of that magnitude.

Dienert and Bennett, however, were persistent. They followed Graham to Oregon and showed up outside his hotel, insisting that he consider starting a national radio program. Graham finally said, “All right fellows, if before midnight tonight I should get $25,000 for the purpose of a radio broadcast, I’ll take that as an answer to prayer and be willing to do a national broadcast.”

He thought there was no way that would happen, but God had answered prayer. They took the step of faith and signed a contract to air the Hour of Decision.

#### The Billy Graham Evangelistic Association

The crew: Billy Graham, Cliff Barrows, and Grady Wilson, didn’t know what to do with the $25,000. They didn’t have a separate corporate bank account or even a board of directors. That’s when the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association (BGEA) was founded. Billy called his business manager at Northwestern School, who filed documents establishing the BGEA.

For thirteen weeks, the American Broadcasting Company would broadcast the Hour of Decision on their coast-to-coast network. They started airing their program during Graham’s Atlanta Crusade. “Clearly, the Lord was setting our course for the immediate future,” said Graham. “In one year between Los Angeles and Atlanta, we had developed an organization, a radio broadcast, a film ministry, a financial policy, and a compatible Team. Now we needed to find out if all these things would work.”

Hour of Decision aired for 60 years, turning into The Hour of Decision Online with the advancements in technology. Continuing to use every means possible to share the Good News of the Gospel, BGEA’s audio team began developing more and more ways to be heard.

Today, they produce radio spots for advertising, as well as a number of online and broadcast programs such as Fearless with Cissie Graham Lynch, GPS: God. People. Stories. and Billy Graham Minute.

#### Satellite Radio: SiriusXM

Most recently, the BGEA has partnered with SiriusXM to have their own channel on satellite radio. “The Billy Graham Channel” on SiriusXM channel 460 is headlined by the inspiring messages of Billy Graham, the late world-renowned Christian evangelist, and features his timeless sermons from his many years in ministry.
